existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` is locally replaced/remodeled as R6 `Ingredient`; hard migration issues include resource identity, required modifier `status`, manufacturer wrapping, mandatory `substance`, `CodeableReference`, removal/collapse of `specifiedSubstance`, and strength choice remodeling. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official cross-version ConceptMap.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is a structural transform, not a version-label update. Systems must instantiate R6 `Ingredient`, add a lifecycle `status`, move R4 `manufacturer` references under `manufacturer.manufacturer`, convert R4 CodeableConcept substance fields into R6 CodeableReference concepts or references, and rewrite strength fields to R6 choice properties. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for R6-only fields such as `for`, `function`, manufacturer role, non-Ratio strengths, SubstanceDefinition references, and text strengths.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable structural differences because they are directly visible in the local StructureDefinitions and package index. Confidence is medium for exact business-intent mapping from R4 `specifiedSubstance` to R6 `Ingredient.substance` because no official diff, narrative rationale, or ConceptMap was available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductIngredient has a resource-identity break: R4 MedicinalProductIngredient is absent in R6 and appears replaced by Ingredient. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 96/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

8 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.title: R4 MedicinalProductIngredient is absent in R6 and appears replaced by Ingredient
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the resourceType, canonical URL, REST type endpoint, parser registration, generated class name, and type switches change from MedicinalProductIngredient to Ingredient; strict instances are also old-valid/new-invalid until transformed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R4 `specifiedSubstance` branch is removed/collapsed, with unclear handling for repeated specified substances and confidentiality
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `specifiedSubstance` use elements absent from R6; direct migration can also cause R6-to-R4 loss or semantic loss for group, confidentiality, and repeated entries.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `referenceStrength.substance` becomes required and reference-strength values use choice serialization
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 referenceStrength entries that omit `substance` fail R6; R4 strength fields also need choice-property conversion, and R6 Quantity or SubstanceDefinition references may be lossy when exported to R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `substance` becomes mandatory and its code changes from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-origin records without `substance` fail R6, and R4 CodeableConcept JSON copied directly to `Ingredient.substance.code` has the wrong CodeableReference shape; R6 reference-only substances can also cause R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 Ingredient adds required modifier `status` with required publication-status binding
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-origin Ingredient records without a newly supplied status fail R6 cardinality and required-binding validation; runtime consumers must also account for the modifier semantics.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `manufacturer` changes from direct Organization Reference to a backbone with manufacturer role
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: serializers and generated clients must move from `manufacturer[n].reference` to `manufacturer[n].manufacturer.reference`; copied R4 JSON is also old-valid/new-invalid at that path.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Strength presentation and concentration fields become choice elements and low-limit fields are removed
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R4 fields such as `presentation` and `concentration` must become choice-suffixed R6 properties; low-limit fields must be represented as RatioRange or otherwise preserved, and some R6-native strength forms are R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: New `ing-1` invariant constrains allergen use with SubstanceDefinition references
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: only enriched R4-to-R6 migrations that use `substance.code.reference` and keep `allergenicIndicator=true` become invalid; direct concept-based migrations remain valid for this constraint.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds optional fields with no clear R4 representation
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-native data in these optional fields may not fit R4 without extensions or dropping values, but R4-to-R6 validation is not harmed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
